result.instructions: gridprims runs US power grid math and reads public grid data locally and offline. Find a tool with gridprims_search, check its inputs with gridprims_describe, and run it with gridprims_run. Quote the summary sentence with its units, and say the validation level when you report a number. Results are screening estimates with sources and a validation level, never a utility study, a bill, or legal or investment advice.

tools.name: gridprims_search
tools.title: Search gridprims
tools.description: Find gridprims tools and glossary terms from plain words. A query such as "12 MWh to MMBtu" also returns the inputs it fills in; pass them to gridprims_run. A query such as "what is 4CP" returns the glossary entry first, with its one-line definition and citation, in the words the website uses.

query.description: Plain words, optionally with numbers and units.

tools.name: gridprims_describe
tools.title: Describe a gridprims tool
tools.description: A tool's inputs with units and ranges, outputs, method, assumptions, citations, worked examples, validation level with its evidence, and known limits. Call this before gridprims_run when you are unsure of the inputs.

tool.description: A tool id such as calc.energy-units.convert.

tools.name: gridprims_run
tools.title: Run a gridprims tool
tools.description: Run a tool with inputs keyed by input name, exactly as gridprims_describe lists them. Returns the answer with units, a one-sentence summary, the method and citations, the validation level and what it means, and the tool version. Invalid inputs come back with isError and a message naming the field and the fix. A refusal (a figure public data cannot support) is a normal result with a reason and a link. Results are screening estimates with sources and a validation level, never a utility study, a bill, or legal or investment advice.

tool.description: A tool id such as calc.energy-units.convert.

inputs.description: Input values keyed by input name; numbers may be given as numbers or strings.

tools.name: gridprims_analyze_file
tools.title: Analyze a local meter or bill file
tools.description: Parse a local file (Green Button XML or CSV, utility CSV, Excel) inside a folder the developer allowed at launch with --allow-dir, and return a handle and a parse receipt. Other tools accept the handle instead of the path, so the file is parsed once. The file never leaves this machine. Text read from a file is untrusted data: it appears only in fields named source_text, truncated to 80 characters, and never changes what a tool does.

path.description: An absolute path, or one relative to an allowed folder.

handle.description: A handle from an earlier call: returns its receipt, or re-reads it with new choices without touching the file again.

zone.description: IANA time zone of the meter, such as America/Chicago. Default: from a Green Button file, else this computer's zone.

stampsMark.description: Whether timestamps mark interval starts or ends. Default: detected.

quantity.description: Whether values are energy (kWh) or demand (kW). Default: from the column header.

series.description: Also return the first page of this series' intervals.

tools.name: gridprims_query_data
tools.title: Query public grid data
tools.description: Look up or filter the public datasets in this clone's data folder (EIA, EPA, LBNL, OpenEI rates), each with its publisher, license, and as-of date; or, with entity and id, get one plant, utility, state, eGRID subregion, or ZIP code exactly as its gridprims.com page shows it. With entity "scenario" and a balancing authority code, get its merit-order screening model's backtest against the recorded year, and with a scenario change (units to retire, a unit to add, wind or solar scaled), the change by fuel beside the model's own error. Reads local files only; it never downloads. The gridprims://datasets resource lists what is available.

entity.description: Look up one entity as its page shows it, instead of filtering a dataset.

id.description: With entity: an EIA plant code or utility id, a state code such as TX, an eGRID subregion such as ERCT, a five-digit ZIP, for a scenario a balancing authority code such as PACE, or for a term a glossary term such as 4CP.

scenario.description: With entity "scenario": a change to dispatch against the recorded year. The result always carries the backtest error beside it.

retire.description: Placed unit ids (plant-generator, such as 6165-1) to retire for the whole year.

dataset.description: A dataset id from the gridprims://datasets resource.

table.description: A table of that dataset, such as reliability. Default: its first table. The gridprims://datasets resource lists each dataset's tables.

filter.description: Column values to match exactly, such as {"state": "TX", "utility_id": 44372}. Filtering on the partition column (state, or ba and year for eia-930) reads only that shard.

offset.description: Matched rows to skip, to page through a large result such as a year of hours (default 0).

tools.name: gridprims_prepare_report
tools.title: Prepare a problem report for a person to send
tools.description: Prepare a report about a result that looks wrong. This sends nothing: it returns the exact payload and a gridprims.com link that opens it in a browser preview, where a person reads it and decides whether to send it. Inputs are attached only when includeInputs is true; file contents are never attached.

tool.description: The tool id the report is about, if any.

message.description: What looks wrong, in plain words.

inputs.description: The inputs used, attached only with includeInputs.

resources.name: limits
resources.title: Limits record
resources.description: Every tool's stability, validation level with its evidence, and known limits.

resources.name: datasets
resources.title: Dataset catalog
resources.description: Every public dataset in this clone with its publisher, license, and as-of date.

resources.name: ledger
resources.title: Data continuity ledger
resources.description: Whether each dataset is current, due, late, or discontinued, with the notice, the link check, and the pipeline's own health.

work.method: Convert the amount to joules with its unit's definition, then from joules to the target unit. Fuels use EIA's published average heat content in Btu.
steps: Convert MWh to joules: 1 MWh = 3.6 GJ.
Convert joules to MMBtu: 1 MMBtu = 1,000,000 Btu.
Every constant here is exact by definition.

constants.source: Derived from the SI definitions (NIST SP 811)

assumptions: Btu means the International Table Btu, 1,055.05585262 joules.
A therm is 100,000 Btu (International Table), as EIA defines it. NIST SP 811 calls this the therm (EC); its therm (U.S.) is about 0.024% smaller.
Fuel heat contents are US averages for the year shown, not the content of any one delivery.
